How signals work

A signal means the pick gate promoted this game: the model's bias-adjusted number, pulled 30% toward the market, still disagrees with the market — and a concrete, checkable reason (like a key injury) backs it. Strong signal and Lean are rare by design. Most games get no signal at all, which is the honest answer when there's no edge; a raw gap alone never earns a badge. New model variants are tracked separately from the main model.

Signals

Every game where our number meaningfully disagrees with the books — the watchlist we're grading over time.

Picks

Biggest gaps between our number and the books, ranked. Each row is the model's read — you decide what to do with it.

How picks are ranked

Overs and Unders rank games where the model’s total differs from the market by at least 2.5 points. Spreads rank games where the model’s spread differs by at least 3 points. Same thresholds as the Lean signal.

How we’re doing

Every finished game lands here with the model's projected margin and total beside the final score.

We score ourselves after each game: “off by 3” means our predicted total was 3 points from the final. Lower is better.

About this tab

"You vs model" compares your line to our pregame total and the market total when that data is present — a "—" means it wasn't logged for that bet. Projections reuse the same pace math as the Games tab. Cash-out numbers are position-management info only.

How it works

Signals, simply

Welcome to Line Lab

We build computer models that predict sports scores — then grade every prediction after the game to see how the models are doing.

Our number vs the books

For every game we show two numbers: what our model predicts, and what the sportsbooks say. A big disagreement alone is not a signal — we only flag a game when the model's number disagrees for a concrete, checkable reason.

Signals, simply

Most games get no signal — no edge stood out. On rare games the model flags a Strong signal or a Lean, when its number disagrees with the market for a concrete, checkable reason. Every flag is the model's read — you decide.

We show our work

After every game we publish how far off we were. “Off by 3” means our predicted total was 3 points from the real final score. Lower is better — and we always show our average miss next to the market's.

About Line Lab

The honest version

What this is

Line Lab is every line, every game, with the numbers behind the call. Every signal is the model's read on that game — you decide what it means.

How we keep ourselves honest

We log our number for every game before it starts and grade it after the final. Wins and misses are both published on the Results tab. Model changes are written up in the lab notebook below the results.

Its limits

Models don't watch the games. They miss injuries that break late, weather that moves, and matchups that numbers can't see. A signal is a starting point for your own check — matchup, injuries, pace, conditions — never the whole answer.
